question.html:
Question 4
?

The point Q with coordinates (2,−4) lies on the curve y=f(x). Which of the following points must lie on y=f(−x)?

a
(−2,4)
b
(−4,2)
c
(2,4)
d
(−4,−2)
e
(−2,−4)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The transformation y=f(−x) reflects the curve y=f(x) in the y-axis.

First, notice that the point P(2,−4) lies 2 units to the right from the y-axis. So, under the action of the transformation, this point will be reflected 2 units to the left from the y-axis.

We conclude that the point (−2,−4) must lie on the graph of y=f(−x).
question.knowledge_point: Finding a Point that Lies on a Transformed Function

solution.reasoning: The transformation y=f(-x) reflects points across the y-axis: (x,y) becomes (-x,y). Therefore (2,-4) becomes (-2,-4), option e. No captured Math Academy answer or grade establishes this question's key.

feedback.name: Question 4
feedback.problem: The point $Q$ with coordinates $(2,-4)$ lies on the curve $y=f(x).$ Which of the following points must lie on $y=f(-x)?$
feedback.worked_solution:
The transformation $y=f(-x)$ reflects the curve $y=f(x)$ in the $y$-axis.

First, notice that the point $P(2,-4)$ lies $2$ units to the *right* from the $y$-axis. So, under the action of the transformation, this point will be reflected $2$ units to the *left* from the $y$-axis.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14224557/assets/456a145820b2a36693df572b49064332a18a2e79c35f2a0e3240b9995660c9a5.png)

We conclude that the point $(-2,-4)$ must lie on the graph of $y=f(-x).$

questions.name: Question 1
questions.problem:
Consider the vector field $F$ and the surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v),$ where

$$
F(x,y,z)=⟨{z}^{2},\,{y}^{2},\,x⟩,\,r(u,v)=⟨{u}^{2},\,v,\,u⟩,\,(u,v)\in D⊂{R}^{2}.
$$

If the flux of $F$ across $S$ with respect to $n$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{D}\boxed{}\,\text{d}A
$$

what is the missing expression?

*Hint: You can use the fact that ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}=⟨-1,\,0,\,2u⟩.$*
questions.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A.
$$

Notice we are told that the fundamental vector product for our surface is

$$
{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}=⟨-1,\,0,\,2u⟩.
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & =⟨{z}^{2},\,{y}^{2},\,x⟩{|}_{x={u}^{2}\,y=v\,z=u} \\  & =⟨{u}^{2},\,{v}^{2},\,{u}^{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the dot product of $F$ and ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨{u}^{2},\,{v}^{2},\,{u}^{2}⟩\cdot ⟨-1,\,0,\,2u⟩ \\  & ={u}^{2}\cdot (-1)+{v}^{2}\cdot 0+{u}^{2}\cdot 2u \\  & =2{u}^{3}-{u}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\,2{u}^{3}-{u}^{2}\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.name: Question 2
questions.problem:
Consider the vector field $F$ and the surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v),$ where

$$
F(x,y,z)=⟨2x,\,2y,\,z⟩,\,r(u,v)=⟨{u}^{2},\,-uv,\,{v}^{2}⟩,\,(u,v)\in D⊂{R}^{2}.
$$

If the flux of $F$ across $S$ with respect to $n$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{D}\boxed{}\,\text{d}A
$$

what is the missing expression?

*Hint: You can use the fact that ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}=⟨-2{v}^{2},\,-4uv,\,-2{u}^{2}⟩.$*
questions.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A.
$$

Notice we are told that the fundamental vector product for our surface is

$$
{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}=⟨-2{v}^{2},\,-4uv,\,-2{u}^{2}⟩.
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & =⟨2x,\,2y,\,z⟩{|}_{x={u}^{2}\,y=-uv\,z={v}^{2}} \\  & =⟨2{u}^{2},\,-2uv,\,{v}^{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the dot product of $F$ and ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨2{u}^{2},\,-2uv,\,{v}^{2}⟩\cdot ⟨-2{v}^{2},\,-4uv,\,-2{u}^{2}⟩ \\  & =2{u}^{2}\cdot (-2{v}^{2})+(-2uv)\cdot (-4uv)+{v}^{2}\cdot (-2{u}^{2}) \\  & =-4{u}^{2}{v}^{2}+8{u}^{2}{v}^{2}-2{u}^{2}{v}^{2} \\  & =2{u}^{2}{v}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\,2{u}^{2}{v}^{2}\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.name: Question 3
questions.problem:
Consider the vector field $F$ and the surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v),$ where

$$
F(x,y,z)=⟨1,\,0,\,2⟩,\,r(u,v)=⟨u+v,\,{u}^{2}+2v,\,{u}^{3}+3v⟩,\,(u,v)\in D⊂{R}^{2}.
$$

If the flux of $F$ across $S$ with respect to $n$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{D}a{u}^{2}+bu+c\,\text{d}A
$$

what is the value of $a+b+c?$
questions.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A.
$$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u+v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}({u}^{2}+2v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}({u}^{3}+3v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,2u,\,3{u}^{2}⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u+v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}({u}^{2}+2v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}({u}^{3}+3v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,2,\,3⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 2u & 3{u}^{2} \\ 1 & 2 & 3\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}2u & 3{u}^{2} \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & 3{u}^{2} \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 2u \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨6u-6{u}^{2},\,3{u}^{2}-3,\,2-2u⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & =⟨1,\,0,\,2⟩{|}_{x=u+v\,y={u}^{2}+2v\,z={u}^{3}+3v} \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,2⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the dot product of $F$ and ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨1,\,0,\,2⟩\cdot ⟨6u-6{u}^{2},\,3{u}^{2}-3,\,2-2u⟩ \\  & =1\cdot (6u-6{u}^{2})+0\cdot (3{u}^{2}-3)+2\cdot (2-2u) \\  & =6u-6{u}^{2}+4-4u \\  & =-6{u}^{2}+2u+4.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(-6)\cdot {u}^{2}+2\cdot u+4\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, 

$$
a+b+c=-6+2+4=0.
$$

questions.name: Question 4
questions.problem:
Consider the vector field $F$ and the surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v),$ where

$$
F(x,y,z)=⟨2x+y,\,2z,\,y+z⟩,\,r(u,v)=⟨-{u}^{2},\,2{u}^{2}-{v}^{2},\,{v}^{2}⟩,\,(u,v)\in D⊂{R}^{2}.
$$

If the flux of $F$ across $S$ with respect to $n$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{D}\boxed{}\,\text{d}A
$$

what is the missing expression?

*Hint: You can use the fact that ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}=⟨8uv,\,4uv,\,4uv⟩.$*
questions.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A.
$$

Notice we are told that the fundamental vector product for our surface is

$$
{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}=⟨8uv,\,4uv,\,4uv⟩.
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & =⟨2x+y,\,2z,\,y+z⟩{|}_{x=-{u}^{2}\,y=2{u}^{2}-{v}^{2}\,z={v}^{2}} \\  & =⟨2(-{u}^{2})+(2{u}^{2}-{v}^{2}),\,2({v}^{2}),\,(2{u}^{2}-{v}^{2})+{v}^{2}⟩ \\  & =⟨-{v}^{2},\,2{v}^{2},\,2{u}^{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the dot product of $F$ and ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨-{v}^{2},\,2{v}^{2},\,2{u}^{2}⟩\cdot ⟨8uv,\,4uv,\,4uv⟩ \\  & =(-{v}^{2})\cdot 8uv+2{v}^{2}\cdot 4uv+2{u}^{2}\cdot 4uv \\  & =-8u{v}^{3}+8u{v}^{3}+8{u}^{3}v \\  & =8{u}^{3}v.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\,8{u}^{3}v\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.name: Question 5
questions.problem:
Consider the vector field $F$ and the surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v),$ where

$$
F(x,y,z)=⟨3x,\,3y,\,z⟩,\,r(u,v)=⟨u\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,u\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,{u}^{2}⟩,\,(u,v)\in D⊂{R}^{2}.
$$

If the flux of $F$ across $S$ with respect to $n$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{D}\boxed{}\,\text{d}A
$$

what is the missing expression?

*Hint: You can use the fact that ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}=⟨-2{u}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,-2{u}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,u⟩.$*
questions.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A.
$$

Notice we are told that the fundamental vector product for our surface is

$$
{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}=⟨-2{u}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,-2{u}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,u⟩.
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & =⟨3x,\,3y,\,z⟩{|}_{x=u\operatorname{cos}⁡v\,y=u\operatorname{sin}⁡v\,z={u}^{2}} \\  & =⟨3u\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,3u\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,{u}^{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the dot product of $F$ and ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨3u\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,3u\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,{u}^{2}⟩\cdot ⟨-2{u}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,-2{u}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,u⟩ \\  & =3u\operatorname{cos}⁡v\cdot (-2{u}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡v)+3u\operatorname{sin}⁡v\cdot (-2{u}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡v)+{u}^{2}\cdot u \\  & =-6{u}^{3}({cos}^{2}⁡v+{sin}^{2}⁡v)+{u}^{3} \\  & =-5{u}^{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\,-5{u}^{3}\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.name: Question 6
questions.problem:
Evaluate the surface integral

$$
{∬}_{S}⟨x,\,y,\,-z⟩\cdot \text{d}S
$$

where the parametric surface $S$ is defined by

$$
r(u,v)=⟨u+v,\,v-u,\,uv⟩
$$

over the domain $D=\{(u,v)\,:\,-2\le u\le 0,\,0\le v\le 1\}.$

*Hint: You can use the fact that ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}=⟨-u-v,\,v-u,\,2⟩.$*
questions.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A.
$$

We're given that the fundamental vector product for our surface is

$$
{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}=⟨-u-v,\,v-u,\,2⟩.
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & ={⟨x,\,y,\,-z⟩|}_{x=u+v\,y=v-u\,z=uv} \\  & =⟨u+v,\,v-u,\,-uv⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we calculate the dot product of $F$ and ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨u+v,\,v-u,\,-uv⟩\cdot ⟨-u-v,\,v-u,\,2⟩ \\  & =(u+v)\cdot (-u-v)+(v-u)\cdot (v-u)+(-uv)\cdot 2 \\  & =-{u}^{2}-2uv-{v}^{2}+{v}^{2}-2uv+{u}^{2}-2uv \\  & =-6uv\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral evaluates to

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}⟨x,\,y,\,-z⟩\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(-6uv)\,\text{d}A \\  & =-6{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{-2}^{0}uv\,\text{d}u\,\text{d}v \\  & =-6{\int }_{0}^{1}v\,\text{d}v{\int }_{-2}^{0}u\,\text{d}u \\  & =-6\cdot [\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2}]_{0}^{1}\cdot {[\frac{1}{2}{u}^{2}]}_{-2}^{0} \\  & =-6\cdot \frac{1}{2}\cdot (-2) \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.name: Question 7
questions.problem:
Evaluate the surface integral

$$
{∬}_{S}⟨-x-z,\,x-y,\,-z⟩\cdot \text{d}S
$$

where the parametric surface $S$ is defined by the equations

$$
r(u,v)=⟨u+v,\,v-u,\,-v⟩
$$

for $-1\le u\le 0$ and $0\le v\le 1.$
questions.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A.
$$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u+v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v-u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(-v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,-1,\,0⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u+v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v-u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(-v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,1,\,-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & -1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}|,-|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}|,|\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,1,\,2⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & ={⟨-x-z,\,x-y,\,-z⟩|}_{x=u+v\,y=v-u\,z=-v} \\  & =⟨-(u+v)-(-v),\,u+v-(v-u),\,-(-v)⟩ \\  & =⟨-u,\,2u,\,v⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the dot product of $F$ and ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨-u,\,2u,\,v⟩\cdot ⟨1,\,1,\,2⟩ \\  & =(-u)\cdot 1+2u\cdot 1+v\cdot 2 \\  & =-u+2u+2v \\  & =u+2v\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral evaluates to

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}⟨-x-z,\,x-y,\,-z⟩\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(u+2v)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}{\int }_{0}^{1}(u+2v)\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}[uv+{v}^{2}]_{v=0}^{v=1}\,\text{d}u \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}(u+1)\text{d}u \\  & ={[\frac{1}{2}{u}^{2}+u]}_{-1}^{0} \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}+1 \\  & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.name: Question 8
questions.problem:
Evaluate the surface integral

$$
{∬}_{S}⟨2x,\,\frac{xz}{3}-2y,\,2z⟩\cdot \text{d}S
$$

where the parametric surface $S$ is defined by

$$
r(u,v)=⟨2u-1,\,uv,\,3v⟩
$$

over the domain $D=\{(u,v)\,:\,0\le u\le 1,\,-1\le v\le 2\}.$

*Hint: You can use the fact that ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}=⟨3v,\,-6,\,2u⟩.$*
questions.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A.
$$

We're given that the fundamental vector product for our surface is

$$
{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}=⟨3v,\,-6,\,2u⟩.
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & ={⟨2x,\,\frac{xz}{3}-2y,\,2z⟩|}_{x=2u-1\,y=uv\,z=3v} \\  & =⟨2(2u-1),\,\frac{(2u-1)(3v)}{3}-2uv,\,2(3v)⟩ \\  & =⟨4u-2,\,-v,\,6v⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we calculate the dot product of $F$ and ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨4u-2,\,-v,\,6v⟩\cdot ⟨3v,\,-6,\,2u⟩ \\  & =(4u-2)\cdot 3v+(-v)\cdot (-6)+6v\cdot 2u \\  & =12uv-6v+6v+12uv \\  & =24uv.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral evaluates to

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}⟨2x,\,\frac{xz}{3}-2y,\,2z⟩\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}24uv\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}24uv\,\text{d}u\text{d}v \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{2}[12{u}^{2}v]_{0}^{1}\,\text{d}v \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{2}12v\,\text{d}v \\  & =[6{v}^{2}]_{-1}^{2} \\  & =6({2}^{2}-(-1)^{2}) \\  & =18.\end{aligned}
$$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}({u}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(uv)⟩ \\  & =⟨2u,\,0,\,v⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}({u}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(uv)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,u⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 2u & 0 & v \\ 0 & 1 & u\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & v \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}|,-|\begin{aligned}2u & v \\ 0 & u\end{aligned}|,|\begin{aligned}2u & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨-v,\,-2{u}^{2},\,2u⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & ={⟨3,\,z,\,y⟩|}_{x={u}^{2}\,y=v\,z=uv} \\  & =⟨3,\,uv,\,v⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the dot product of $F$ and ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨3,\,uv,\,v⟩\cdot ⟨-v,\,-2{u}^{2},\,2u⟩ \\  & =3\cdot (-v)+uv\cdot (-2{u}^{2})+v\cdot 2u \\  & =-3v-2{u}^{3}v+2uv\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral evaluates to

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}⟨3,\,z,\,y⟩\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(-3v-2{u}^{3}v+2uv)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{-1}^{1}(-3v-2{u}^{3}v+2uv)\,\text{d}u\,\text{d}v \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{[-3uv-\frac{1}{2}{u}^{4}v+{u}^{2}v]}_{u=-1}^{u=1}\,\text{d}v \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(-6v)\text{d}v \\  & =[-3{v}^{2}]_{0}^{1} \\  & =-3.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.name: Question 10
questions.problem:
Evaluate the surface integral

$$
{∬}_{S}⟨3z,\,-2x,\,-y⟩\cdot \text{d}S
$$

where the parametric surface $S$ is defined by the equations

$$
r(u,v)=⟨-v,\,-u,\,{u}^{2}⟩
$$

for $0\le u\le 1$ and $0\le v\le 1.$
questions.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A.
$$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(-v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(-u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}({u}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,-1,\,2u⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(-v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(-u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}({u}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,\,0,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 0 & -1 & 2u \\ -1 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}-1 & 2u \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}|,-|\begin{aligned}0 & 2u \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}|,|\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,-2u,\,-1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & ={⟨3z,\,-2x,\,-y⟩|}_{x=-v\,y=-u\,z={u}^{2}} \\  & =⟨3{u}^{2},\,-2(-v),\,-(-u)⟩ \\  & =⟨3{u}^{2},\,2v,\,u⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we calculate the dot product of $F$ and ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨3{u}^{2},\,2v,\,u⟩\cdot ⟨0,\,-2u,\,-1⟩ \\  & =3{u}^{2}\cdot 0+2v\cdot (-2u)+u\cdot (-1) \\  & =-4uv-u\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral evaluates to

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}⟨3z,\,-2x,\,-y⟩\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(-4uv-u)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}(-4uv-u)\,\text{d}u\,\text{d}v \\  & =-{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}(4uv+u)\,\text{d}u\,\text{d}v \\  & =-{\int }_{0}^{1}{[2{u}^{2}v+\frac{1}{2}{u}^{2}]}_{u=0}^{u=1}\,\text{d}v \\  & =-{\int }_{0}^{1}(2v+\frac{1}{2})\text{d}v \\  & =-{[{v}^{2}+\frac{1}{2}v]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =-\frac{3}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.name:
Example: 
                    Expressing Flux Through a Surface as a Double Integral
canonical_examples.problem:
Consider the vector field $\mathbf F$ and the surface $S$ with parametrization $\mathbf r(u,v),$ where

$$
\mathbf{F}(x,y,z) =\left\langle x+y,\: x-y,\: xyz \right\rangle, \quad \mathbf{r}(u,v) = \left\langle u^2,\: v^2 ,\: 1 \right\rangle, \quad (u,v)\in D\subset \mathbb{R}^2.
$$

If the flux of $\mathbf F$ across $S$ with respect to $\mathbf{n}$ is given by

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14224561/assets/d7b8d89cae048a9cd5e04299bebdcb3a5d5d21ac6d5a31c48482aa00ca71517c.svg)

what is the missing expression?
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $\mathbf{r}(u,v)$ for $(u,v) \in D,$ the flux of a vector field $\mathbf{F}$ over $S$ is given by

$$
\iint\limits_S \mathbf{F} \cdot \textrm{d}\mathbf{S}
=
\iint\limits_S \mathbf{F} \cdot \mathbf{n} \,\textrm{d}S
=
\iint\limits_D \mathbf{F}(\mathbf{r}(u,v)) \cdot (\mathbf{r}'_u \times \mathbf{r}'_v) \,\textrm{d}A.
$$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}({u}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}({v}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(1)⟩ \\  & =⟨2u,\,0,\,0⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}({u}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}({v}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(1)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,2v,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 2u & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 2v & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 2v & 0\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}2u & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}2u & 0 \\ 0 & 2v\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,0,\,4uv⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $\mathbf{r}(u,v)$ into $\mathbf{F}(x,y,z){:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & =⟨x+y,\,x-y,\,xyz⟩{|}_{x={u}^{2}\,y={v}^{2}\,z=1} \\  & =⟨{u}^{2}+{v}^{2},\,{u}^{2}-{v}^{2},\,{u}^{2}{v}^{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the dot product of $\mathbf{F}$ and $\mathbf{r}'_u \times \mathbf{r}'_v{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨{u}^{2}+{v}^{2},\,{u}^{2}-{v}^{2},\,{u}^{2}{v}^{2}⟩\cdot ⟨0,\,0,\,4uv⟩ \\  & =({u}^{2}+{v}^{2})\cdot 0+({u}^{2}-{v}^{2})\cdot 0+{u}^{2}{v}^{2}\cdot 4uv \\  & =4{u}^{3}{v}^{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\,4{u}^{3}{v}^{3}\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.name:
Example: 
                    Evaluating Flux Through a Surface
canonical_examples.problem:
Evaluate the surface integral

$$
\iint\limits_S \left\langle z, \: x, \: y \right\rangle \cdot \textrm{d}\mathbf{S}
$$

where the parametric surface $S$ is defined by the equations

$$
\mathbf{r}(u,v) = \left\langle 1+2u+v, \: u+v, \: u-v \right\rangle
$$

for $0 \leq u \leq 2$ and $0 \leq v \leq 1.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $\mathbf{r}(u,v)$ for $(u,v) \in D,$ the flux of a vector field $\mathbf{F}$ over $S$ is given by

$$
\iint\limits_S \mathbf{F} \cdot \textrm{d}\mathbf{S}
=
\iint\limits_S \mathbf{F} \cdot \mathbf{n} \,\textrm{d}S
=
\iint\limits_D \mathbf{F}(\mathbf{r}(u,v)) \cdot (\mathbf{r}'_u \times \mathbf{r}'_v) \,\textrm{d}A.
$$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(1+2u+v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u+v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u-v)⟩ \\  & =⟨2,\,1,\,1⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(1+2u+v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u+v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u-v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,1,\,-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 2 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}|,-|\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}|,|\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨-2,\,3,\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $\mathbf{r}(u,v)$ into $\mathbf{F}(x,y,z){:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & ={⟨z,\,x,\,y⟩|}_{x=1+2u+v\,y=u+v\,z=u-v} \\  & =⟨u-v,\,1+2u+v,\,u+v⟩\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨u-v,\,1+2u+v,\,u+v⟩\cdot ⟨-2,\,3,\,1⟩ \\  & =(u-v)\cdot (-2)+(1+2u+v)\cdot 3+(u+v)\cdot 1 \\  & =-2u+2v+3+6u+3v+u+v \\  & =5u+6v+3\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral evaluates to

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}⟨z,\,x,\,y⟩\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(5u+6v+3)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}(5u+6v+3)\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}[5uv+3{v}^{2}+3v]_{v=0}^{v=1}\,\text{d}u \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}(5u+6)\,\text{d}u \\  & ={[\frac{5}{2}{u}^{2}+6u]}_{0}^{2} \\  & =10+12 \\  & =22.\end{aligned}
$$

tutorials.name: Introduction
tutorials.problem:
Recall that the flux of the vector field $\mathbf F$ across a smooth, orientable surface $S$ with respect to the unit normal vector $\mathbf{n}$ is given by 

$$
\iint\limits_S \mathbf F \cdot \textrm{d} \mathbf{S}
=
\iint\limits_S  \mathbf F \cdot {\color{blue}\mathbf{n}} \,\textrm{d}S,
$$

where ${\color{blue}\mathbf{n}}$ is a unit normal vector that defines the orientation of the surface.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14224561/assets/9aa63a1e4f1d278cef6c53600e8fb9c60829de972ba7409afdc32837ecbc3e07.png)

If $S$ is given by a parametric equation of the form 

$$
\mathbf{r}=\mathbf{r}(u,v), \qquad (u,v)\in D\subseteq \mathbb{R}^2,
$$

we can determine the unit normal vector using the fundamental product as follows:

$$
{\color{blue}\mathbf{n}} = \dfrac{\mathbf{r}'_u \times \mathbf{r}'_v}{\| \mathbf{r}'_u \times \mathbf{r}'_v \|}
$$

 

Substituting this into the formula for the flux, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S \\  & ={∬}_{S}F\cdot \frac{{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}}{‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖}\,\text{d}S \\  & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot \frac{{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}}{‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖}\,‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, if $S$ is a smooth, orientable surface given in parametric form by $\mathbf{r}=\mathbf{r}(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2,$ then the flux of the vector field $\mathbf{F}$ across $S$ is given by

$$
\iint\limits_S \mathbf F \cdot \textrm{d} \mathbf{S} = \iint\limits_D  \mathbf F(\mathbf{r}(u,v)) \cdot (\mathbf{r}'_u \times \mathbf{r}'_v) \: \textrm{d}A.
$$

Let's see some examples.

observed_steps.name: Example: Expressing Flux Through a Surface as a Double Integral
observed_steps.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $\mathbf{r}(u,v)$ for $(u,v) \in D,$ the flux of a vector field $\mathbf{F}$ over $S$ is given by

$$
\iint\limits_S \mathbf{F} \cdot \textrm{d}\mathbf{S}
=
\iint\limits_S \mathbf{F} \cdot \mathbf{n} \,\textrm{d}S
=
\iint\limits_D \mathbf{F}(\mathbf{r}(u,v)) \cdot (\mathbf{r}'_u \times \mathbf{r}'_v) \,\textrm{d}A.
$$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}({u}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}({v}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(1)⟩ \\  & =⟨2u,\,0,\,0⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}({u}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}({v}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(1)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,2v,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 2u & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 2v & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 2v & 0\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}2u & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}2u & 0 \\ 0 & 2v\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,0,\,4uv⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $\mathbf{r}(u,v)$ into $\mathbf{F}(x,y,z){:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & =⟨x+y,\,x-y,\,xyz⟩{|}_{x={u}^{2}\,y={v}^{2}\,z=1} \\  & =⟨{u}^{2}+{v}^{2},\,{u}^{2}-{v}^{2},\,{u}^{2}{v}^{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the dot product of $\mathbf{F}$ and $\mathbf{r}'_u \times \mathbf{r}'_v{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨{u}^{2}+{v}^{2},\,{u}^{2}-{v}^{2},\,{u}^{2}{v}^{2}⟩\cdot ⟨0,\,0,\,4uv⟩ \\  & =({u}^{2}+{v}^{2})\cdot 0+({u}^{2}-{v}^{2})\cdot 0+{u}^{2}{v}^{2}\cdot 4uv \\  & =4{u}^{3}{v}^{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\,4{u}^{3}{v}^{3}\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

question.html:
Question 1
?

Consider the vector field F and the surface S with parametrization r(u,v), where

F(x,y,z)=⟨z2,y2,x⟩,r(u,v)=⟨u2,v,u⟩,(u,v)∈D⊂R2.

If the flux of F across S with respect to n is given by

∬SF⋅dS=∬DAAAAAAAdA

what is the missing expression?

Hint: You can use the fact that ru′×rv′=⟨−1,0,2u⟩.

a
2u2
b
uv2−2v3
c
2u2+uv
d
2u3−u2
e
u2−v2
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

For a surface S with parametrization r(u,v) for (u,v)∈D, the flux of a vector field F over S is given by

∬SF⋅dS=∬SF⋅ndS=∬DF(r(u,v))⋅(ru′×rv′)dA.

Notice we are told that the fundamental vector product for our surface is

ru′×rv′=⟨−1,0,2u⟩.

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of r(u,v) into F(x,y,z):

F(r(u,v))=⟨z2,y2,x⟩|x=u2y=vz=u=⟨u2,v2,u2⟩

Finally, we calculate the dot product of F and ru′×rv′:

F(r(u,v))⋅(ru′×rv′)=⟨u2,v2,u2⟩⋅⟨−1,0,2u⟩=u2⋅(−1)+v2⋅0+u2⋅2u=2u3−u2.

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

∬SF⋅dS=∬DF(r(u,v))⋅(ru′×rv′)dA=∬D2u3−u2dA.

observed_steps.name: Question 2
observed_steps.knowledge_point: Example: Expressing Flux Through a Surface as a Double Integral
observed_steps.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A.
$$

Notice we are told that the fundamental vector product for our surface is

$$
{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}=⟨-2{v}^{2},\,-4uv,\,-2{u}^{2}⟩.
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & =⟨2x,\,2y,\,z⟩{|}_{x={u}^{2}\,y=-uv\,z={v}^{2}} \\  & =⟨2{u}^{2},\,-2uv,\,{v}^{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the dot product of $F$ and ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨2{u}^{2},\,-2uv,\,{v}^{2}⟩\cdot ⟨-2{v}^{2},\,-4uv,\,-2{u}^{2}⟩ \\  & =2{u}^{2}\cdot (-2{v}^{2})+(-2uv)\cdot (-4uv)+{v}^{2}\cdot (-2{u}^{2}) \\  & =-4{u}^{2}{v}^{2}+8{u}^{2}{v}^{2}-2{u}^{2}{v}^{2} \\  & =2{u}^{2}{v}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\,2{u}^{2}{v}^{2}\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

F(x,y,z)=⟨2x,2y,z⟩,r(u,v)=⟨u2,−uv,v2⟩,(u,v)∈D⊂R2.

If the flux of F across S with respect to n is given by

∬SF⋅dS=∬DAAAAAAAdA

a
−2u3v−2uv3
b
u2v−2u2v2+uv2
c
6u2v2
d
2u2v2
e
u3v+uv3

∬SF⋅dS=∬SF⋅ndS=∬DF(r(u,v))⋅(ru′×rv′)dA.

observed_steps.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A.
$$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u+v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}({u}^{2}+2v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}({u}^{3}+3v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,2u,\,3{u}^{2}⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u+v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}({u}^{2}+2v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}({u}^{3}+3v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,2,\,3⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 2u & 3{u}^{2} \\ 1 & 2 & 3\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}2u & 3{u}^{2} \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & 3{u}^{2} \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 2u \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨6u-6{u}^{2},\,3{u}^{2}-3,\,2-2u⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & =⟨1,\,0,\,2⟩{|}_{x=u+v\,y={u}^{2}+2v\,z={u}^{3}+3v} \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,2⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the dot product of $F$ and ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨1,\,0,\,2⟩\cdot ⟨6u-6{u}^{2},\,3{u}^{2}-3,\,2-2u⟩ \\  & =1\cdot (6u-6{u}^{2})+0\cdot (3{u}^{2}-3)+2\cdot (2-2u) \\  & =6u-6{u}^{2}+4-4u \\  & =-6{u}^{2}+2u+4.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(-6)\cdot {u}^{2}+2\cdot u+4\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, 

$$
a+b+c=-6+2+4=0.
$$

Consider the vector field F and the surface S with parametrization r(u,v), where

F(x,y,z)=⟨1,0,2⟩,r(u,v)=⟨u+v,u2+2v,u3+3v⟩,(u,v)∈D⊂R2.

If the flux of F across S with respect to n is given by

∬SF⋅dS=∬Dau2+bu+cdA

what is the value of a+b+c?

a
2
b
−4
c
0

Correct
EXPLANATION

For a surface S with parametrization r(u,v) for (u,v)∈D, the flux of a vector field F over S is given by

∬SF⋅dS=∬SF⋅ndS=∬DF(r(u,v))⋅(ru′×rv′)dA.

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

ru′=⟨∂x∂u,∂y∂u,∂z∂u⟩=⟨∂∂u(u+v),∂∂u(u2+2v),∂∂u(u3+3v)⟩=⟨1,2u,3u2⟩rv′=⟨∂x∂v,∂y∂v,∂z∂v⟩=⟨∂∂v(u+v),∂∂v(u2+2v),∂∂v(u3+3v)⟩=⟨1,2,3⟩

Now, the fundamental vector product is

ru′×rv′=|ijk12u3u2123|=⟨|2u3u223|,−|13u213|,|12u12|⟩=⟨6u−6u2,3u2−3,2−2u⟩.

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of r(u,v) into F(x,y,z):

F(r(u,v))=⟨1,0,2⟩|x=u+vy=u2+2vz=u3+3v=⟨1,0,2⟩.

Finally, we calculate the dot product of F and ru′×rv′:

F(r(u,v))⋅(ru′×rv′)=⟨1,0,2⟩⋅⟨6u−6u2,3u2−3,2−2u⟩=1⋅(6u−6u2)+0⋅(3u2−3)+2⋅(2−2u)=6u−6u2+4−4u=−6u2+2u+4.

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

∬SF⋅dS=∬DF(r(u,v))⋅(ru′×rv′)dA=∬D(−6)⋅u2+2⋅u+4dA.

Finally,

a+b+c=−6+2+4=0.

observed_steps.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A.
$$

Notice we are told that the fundamental vector product for our surface is

$$
{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}=⟨8uv,\,4uv,\,4uv⟩.
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & =⟨2x+y,\,2z,\,y+z⟩{|}_{x=-{u}^{2}\,y=2{u}^{2}-{v}^{2}\,z={v}^{2}} \\  & =⟨2(-{u}^{2})+(2{u}^{2}-{v}^{2}),\,2({v}^{2}),\,(2{u}^{2}-{v}^{2})+{v}^{2}⟩ \\  & =⟨-{v}^{2},\,2{v}^{2},\,2{u}^{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the dot product of $F$ and ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨-{v}^{2},\,2{v}^{2},\,2{u}^{2}⟩\cdot ⟨8uv,\,4uv,\,4uv⟩ \\  & =(-{v}^{2})\cdot 8uv+2{v}^{2}\cdot 4uv+2{u}^{2}\cdot 4uv \\  & =-8u{v}^{3}+8u{v}^{3}+8{u}^{3}v \\  & =8{u}^{3}v.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\,8{u}^{3}v\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

observed_steps.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $\mathbf{r}(u,v)$ for $(u,v) \in D,$ the flux of a vector field $\mathbf{F}$ over $S$ is given by

$$
\iint\limits_S \mathbf{F} \cdot \textrm{d}\mathbf{S}
=
\iint\limits_S \mathbf{F} \cdot \mathbf{n} \,\textrm{d}S
=
\iint\limits_D \mathbf{F}(\mathbf{r}(u,v)) \cdot (\mathbf{r}'_u \times \mathbf{r}'_v) \,\textrm{d}A.
$$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(1+2u+v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u+v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u-v)⟩ \\  & =⟨2,\,1,\,1⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(1+2u+v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u+v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u-v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,1,\,-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 2 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}|,-|\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}|,|\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨-2,\,3,\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $\mathbf{r}(u,v)$ into $\mathbf{F}(x,y,z){:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & ={⟨z,\,x,\,y⟩|}_{x=1+2u+v\,y=u+v\,z=u-v} \\  & =⟨u-v,\,1+2u+v,\,u+v⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we calculate the dot product of $\mathbf{F}$ and $\mathbf{r}'_u \times \mathbf{r}'_v{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨u-v,\,1+2u+v,\,u+v⟩\cdot ⟨-2,\,3,\,1⟩ \\  & =(u-v)\cdot (-2)+(1+2u+v)\cdot 3+(u+v)\cdot 1 \\  & =-2u+2v+3+6u+3v+u+v \\  & =5u+6v+3\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral evaluates to

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}⟨z,\,x,\,y⟩\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(5u+6v+3)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}(5u+6v+3)\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}[5uv+3{v}^{2}+3v]_{v=0}^{v=1}\,\text{d}u \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}(5u+6)\,\text{d}u \\  & ={[\frac{5}{2}{u}^{2}+6u]}_{0}^{2} \\  & =10+12 \\  & =22.\end{aligned}
$$

question.name: Question 6
question.problem:
Evaluate the surface integral

$$
{∬}_{S}⟨x,\,y,\,-z⟩\cdot \text{d}S
$$

where the parametric surface $S$ is defined by

$$
r(u,v)=⟨u+v,\,v-u,\,uv⟩
$$

over the domain $D=\{(u,v)\,:\,-2\le u\le 0,\,0\le v\le 1\}.$

*Hint: You can use the fact that ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}=⟨-u-v,\,v-u,\,2⟩.$*

For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F$ over $S$ is given by

$$

$$

We're given that the fundamental vector product for our surface is

$$
{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}=⟨-u-v,\,v-u,\,2⟩.
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & ={⟨x,\,y,\,-z⟩|}_{x=u+v\,y=v-u\,z=uv} \\  & =⟨u+v,\,v-u,\,-uv⟩\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}⟨x,\,y,\,-z⟩\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(-6uv)\,\text{d}A \\  & =-6{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{-2}^{0}uv\,\text{d}u\,\text{d}v \\  & =-6{\int }_{0}^{1}v\,\text{d}v{\int }_{-2}^{0}u\,\text{d}u \\  & =-6\cdot [\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2}]_{0}^{1}\cdot {[\frac{1}{2}{u}^{2}]}_{-2}^{0} \\  & =-6\cdot \frac{1}{2}\cdot (-2) \\  & =6.\end{aligned}

{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A.
$$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u+v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v-u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(-v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,-1,\,0⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u+v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v-u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(-v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,1,\,-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & -1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}|,-|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}|,|\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,1,\,2⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & ={⟨-x-z,\,x-y,\,-z⟩|}_{x=u+v\,y=v-u\,z=-v} \\  & =⟨-(u+v)-(-v),\,u+v-(v-u),\,-(-v)⟩ \\  & =⟨-u,\,2u,\,v⟩\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨-u,\,2u,\,v⟩\cdot ⟨1,\,1,\,2⟩ \\  & =(-u)\cdot 1+2u\cdot 1+v\cdot 2 \\  & =-u+2u+2v \\  & =u+2v\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}⟨-x-z,\,x-y,\,-z⟩\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(u+2v)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}{\int }_{0}^{1}(u+2v)\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}[uv+{v}^{2}]_{v=0}^{v=1}\,\text{d}u \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}(u+1)\text{d}u \\  & ={[\frac{1}{2}{u}^{2}+u]}_{-1}^{0} \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}+1 \\  & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}

where the parametric surface $S$ is defined by

$$

We're given that the fundamental vector product for our surface is

$$
{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}=⟨3v,\,-6,\,2u⟩.
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & ={⟨2x,\,\frac{xz}{3}-2y,\,2z⟩|}_{x=2u-1\,y=uv\,z=3v} \\  & =⟨2(2u-1),\,\frac{(2u-1)(3v)}{3}-2uv,\,2(3v)⟩ \\  & =⟨4u-2,\,-v,\,6v⟩\end{aligned}

For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F$ over $S$ is given by

$$

$$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}({u}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(uv)⟩ \\  & =⟨2u,\,0,\,v⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}({u}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(uv)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,u⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 2u & 0 & v \\ 0 & 1 & u\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & v \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}|,-|\begin{aligned}2u & v \\ 0 & u\end{aligned}|,|\begin{aligned}2u & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨-v,\,-2{u}^{2},\,2u⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & ={⟨3,\,z,\,y⟩|}_{x={u}^{2}\,y=v\,z=uv} \\  & =⟨3,\,uv,\,v⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the dot product of $F$ and ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨3,\,uv,\,v⟩\cdot ⟨-v,\,-2{u}^{2},\,2u⟩ \\  & =3\cdot (-v)+uv\cdot (-2{u}^{2})+v\cdot 2u \\  & =-3v-2{u}^{3}v+2uv\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral evaluates to

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}⟨3,\,z,\,y⟩\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(-3v-2{u}^{3}v+2uv)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{-1}^{1}(-3v-2{u}^{3}v+2uv)\,\text{d}u\,\text{d}v \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{[-3uv-\frac{1}{2}{u}^{4}v+{u}^{2}v]}_{u=-1}^{u=1}\,\text{d}v \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(-6v)\text{d}v \\  & =[-3{v}^{2}]_{0}^{1} \\  & =-3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral evaluates to

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}⟨3z,\,-2x,\,-y⟩\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(-4uv-u)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}(-4uv-u)\,\text{d}u\,\text{d}v \\  & =-{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}(4uv+u)\,\text{d}u\,\text{d}v \\  & =-{\int }_{0}^{1}{[2{u}^{2}v+\frac{1}{2}{u}^{2}]}_{u=0}^{u=1}\,\text{d}v \\  & =-{\int }_{0}^{1}(2v+\frac{1}{2})\text{d}v \\  & =-{[{v}^{2}+\frac{1}{2}v]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =-\frac{3}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.name: Question 10
question.problem:
Evaluate the surface integral

$$
{∬}_{S}⟨3z,\,-2x,\,-y⟩\cdot \text{d}S
$$

where the parametric surface $S$ is defined by the equations

$$
r(u,v)=⟨-v,\,-u,\,{u}^{2}⟩
$$

for $0\le u\le 1$ and $0\le v\le 1.$
question.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A.
$$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(-v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(-u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}({u}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,-1,\,2u⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(-v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(-u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}({u}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,\,0,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 0 & -1 & 2u \\ -1 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}-1 & 2u \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}|,-|\begin{aligned}0 & 2u \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}|,|\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,-2u,\,-1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & ={⟨3z,\,-2x,\,-y⟩|}_{x=-v\,y=-u\,z={u}^{2}} \\  & =⟨3{u}^{2},\,-2(-v),\,-(-u)⟩ \\  & =⟨3{u}^{2},\,2v,\,u⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we calculate the dot product of $F$ and ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨3{u}^{2},\,2v,\,u⟩\cdot ⟨0,\,-2u,\,-1⟩ \\  & =3{u}^{2}\cdot 0+2v\cdot (-2u)+u\cdot (-1) \\  & =-4uv-u\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral evaluates to

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}⟨3z,\,-2x,\,-y⟩\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(-4uv-u)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}(-4uv-u)\,\text{d}u\,\text{d}v \\  & =-{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}(4uv+u)\,\text{d}u\,\text{d}v \\  & =-{\int }_{0}^{1}{[2{u}^{2}v+\frac{1}{2}{u}^{2}]}_{u=0}^{u=1}\,\text{d}v \\  & =-{\int }_{0}^{1}(2v+\frac{1}{2})\text{d}v \\  & =-{[{v}^{2}+\frac{1}{2}v]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =-\frac{3}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

For a surface S with parametrization r(u,v) for (u,v)∈D, the flux of a vector field F over S is given by ∬SF⋅dS=∬SF⋅ndS=∬DF(r(u,v))⋅(ru′×rv′)dA.

judgments.reasoning: F(r(u,v))=⟨u²,v²,u²⟩, so its dot product with ⟨−1,0,2u⟩ is 2u³−u². This confirms the earlier answer, option d. Math Academy graded that exact submitted value Correct, and its worked solution agrees.

F(r(u,v))=⟨2u²,−2uv,v²⟩, giving the flux integrand −4u²v²+8u²v²−2u²v²=2u²v², option d. This agrees with my earlier answer and Math Academy’s revealed worked solution. The Incorrect grade applies to the captured submission of option a, not to option d.

The cross product is ⟨6u−6u²,3u²−3,2−2u⟩. Dotting with ⟨1,0,2⟩ gives −6u²+2u+4, so a+b+c=0, option c. This agrees with my earlier answer, the submitted value graded Correct, and Math Academy’s worked solution.

Substitution gives F(r(u,v))=⟨−v²,2v²,2u²⟩. Its dot product with ⟨8uv,4uv,4uv⟩ is −8uv³+8uv³+8u³v=8u³v, option e. This agrees with my earlier answer and Math Academy’s worked solution. The Incorrect grade applies to the captured submission of option a, which includes an extra 8uv³ term.

The flux integrand is −6u³cos²v−6u³sin²v+u³=−5u³, using cos²v+sin²v=1. Thus option d is correct, agreeing with my earlier answer, Math Academy’s Correct grade for that submission, and its worked solution.

The flux integrand is −(u+v)²+(v−u)²−2uv=−6uv. Integrating gives −6(−2)(1/2)=6, option e. This agrees with my earlier answer, Math Academy’s Correct grade for the submitted value, and its worked solution.

The cross product is ⟨1,1,2⟩ and F(r(u,v))=⟨−u,2u,v⟩, giving integrand u+2v. Its integral is ∫_{−1}^0(u+1)du=1/2, option a. This agrees with my earlier answer and Math Academy’s worked solution. The Incorrect grade applies to the captured submission of −3/2, option b.

Substitution gives F(r(u,v))=⟨4u−2,−v,6v⟩. Dotting with ⟨3v,−6,2u⟩ yields 24uv, whose integral is 24(1/2)(3/2)=18, option b. This agrees with my earlier answer, Math Academy’s Correct grade for that submission, and its worked solution.

The cross product is ⟨−v,−2u²,2u⟩ and F(r(u,v))=⟨3,uv,v⟩, giving integrand −3v−2u³v+2uv. The odd terms integrate to zero over −1≤u≤1, leaving ∫_0^1−6v dv=−3, option a. This agrees with my earlier answer and Math Academy’s worked solution. The Incorrect grade applies to the captured submission of −1, option b.

The cross product is ⟨0,−2u,−1⟩ and F(r(u,v))=⟨3u²,2v,u⟩, giving integrand −4uv−u. Integrating over [0,1]² yields −1−1/2=−3/2, option d. This agrees with my earlier answer, Math Academy’s Correct grade for that submission, and its worked solution.

The missing expression is 4u^{3}v^{3}: r_u×r_v=⟨0,0,4uv⟩ and F(r(u,v))=⟨u²+v²,u²−v²,u²v²⟩, whose dot product is 4u³v³. Math Academy’s worked solution agrees. The earlier mathematical answer was correct, but its invented answer field was unsupported; this example supplies no response fields.

The tangent vectors ⟨2,1,1⟩ and ⟨1,1,−1⟩ have cross product ⟨−2,3,1⟩. Substitution gives F(r(u,v))=⟨u−v,1+2u+v,u+v⟩, so the integrand is 5u+6v+3. Integrating over [0,2]×[0,1] gives 22, agreeing with Math Academy’s worked solution. This example supplies no response fields.

question.name: Question 1
question.problem:
Consider the vector field $F$ and the surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v),$ where

$$
F(x,y,z)=⟨{z}^{2},\,{y}^{2},\,x⟩,\,r(u,v)=⟨{u}^{2},\,v,\,u⟩,\,(u,v)\in D⊂{R}^{2}.
$$

If the flux of $F$ across $S$ with respect to $n$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{D}\boxed{}\,\text{d}A
$$

what is the missing expression?

*Hint: You can use the fact that ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}=⟨-1,\,0,\,2u⟩.$*
question.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A.
$$

Notice we are told that the fundamental vector product for our surface is

$$
{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}=⟨-1,\,0,\,2u⟩.
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & =⟨{z}^{2},\,{y}^{2},\,x⟩{|}_{x={u}^{2}\,y=v\,z=u} \\  & =⟨{u}^{2},\,{v}^{2},\,{u}^{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the dot product of $F$ and ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨{u}^{2},\,{v}^{2},\,{u}^{2}⟩\cdot ⟨-1,\,0,\,2u⟩ \\  & ={u}^{2}\cdot (-1)+{v}^{2}\cdot 0+{u}^{2}\cdot 2u \\  & =2{u}^{3}-{u}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\,2{u}^{3}-{u}^{2}\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

question.html:
Question 1
?

Consider the vector field F and the surface S with parametrization r(u,v), where

F(x,y,z)=⟨z2,y2,x⟩,r(u,v)=⟨u2,v,u⟩,(u,v)∈D⊂R2.

If the flux of F across S with respect to n is given by

∬SF⋅dS=∬DAAAAAAAdA

what is the missing expression?

Hint: You can use the fact that ru′×rv′=⟨−1,0,2u⟩.

a
2u2
b
uv2−2v3
c
2u2+uv
d
2u3−u2
e
u2−v2
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

For a surface S with parametrization r(u,v) for (u,v)∈D, the flux of a vector field F over S is given by

∬SF⋅dS=∬SF⋅ndS=∬DF(r(u,v))⋅(ru′×rv′)dA.

Notice we are told that the fundamental vector product for our surface is

ru′×rv′=⟨−1,0,2u⟩.

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of r(u,v) into F(x,y,z):

F(r(u,v))=⟨z2,y2,x⟩|x=u2y=vz=u=⟨u2,v2,u2⟩

Finally, we calculate the dot product of F and ru′×rv′:

F(r(u,v))⋅(ru′×rv′)=⟨u2,v2,u2⟩⋅⟨−1,0,2u⟩=u2⋅(−1)+v2⋅0+u2⋅2u=2u3−u2.

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

∬SF⋅dS=∬DF(r(u,v))⋅(ru′×rv′)dA=∬D2u3−u2dA.

last_observation.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A.
$$

Notice we are told that the fundamental vector product for our surface is

$$
{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}=⟨-1,\,0,\,2u⟩.
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & =⟨{z}^{2},\,{y}^{2},\,x⟩{|}_{x={u}^{2}\,y=v\,z=u} \\  & =⟨{u}^{2},\,{v}^{2},\,{u}^{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the dot product of $F$ and ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨{u}^{2},\,{v}^{2},\,{u}^{2}⟩\cdot ⟨-1,\,0,\,2u⟩ \\  & ={u}^{2}\cdot (-1)+{v}^{2}\cdot 0+{u}^{2}\cdot 2u \\  & =2{u}^{3}-{u}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\,2{u}^{3}-{u}^{2}\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.name: Question 1
feedback.problem:
Consider the vector field $F$ and the surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v),$ where

$$
F(x,y,z)=⟨{z}^{2},\,{y}^{2},\,x⟩,\,r(u,v)=⟨{u}^{2},\,v,\,u⟩,\,(u,v)\in D⊂{R}^{2}.
$$

If the flux of $F$ across $S$ with respect to $n$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{D}\boxed{}\,\text{d}A
$$

what is the missing expression?

*Hint: You can use the fact that ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}=⟨-1,\,0,\,2u⟩.$*
feedback.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A.
$$

Notice we are told that the fundamental vector product for our surface is

$$
{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}=⟨-1,\,0,\,2u⟩.
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & =⟨{z}^{2},\,{y}^{2},\,x⟩{|}_{x={u}^{2}\,y=v\,z=u} \\  & =⟨{u}^{2},\,{v}^{2},\,{u}^{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the dot product of $F$ and ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨{u}^{2},\,{v}^{2},\,{u}^{2}⟩\cdot ⟨-1,\,0,\,2u⟩ \\  & ={u}^{2}\cdot (-1)+{v}^{2}\cdot 0+{u}^{2}\cdot 2u \\  & =2{u}^{3}-{u}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\,2{u}^{3}-{u}^{2}\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

question.name: Question 2
question.problem:
Consider the vector field $F$ and the surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v),$ where

$$
F(x,y,z)=⟨2x,\,2y,\,z⟩,\,r(u,v)=⟨{u}^{2},\,-uv,\,{v}^{2}⟩,\,(u,v)\in D⊂{R}^{2}.
$$

If the flux of $F$ across $S$ with respect to $n$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{D}\boxed{}\,\text{d}A
$$

what is the missing expression?

*Hint: You can use the fact that ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}=⟨-2{v}^{2},\,-4uv,\,-2{u}^{2}⟩.$*
question.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A.
$$

Notice we are told that the fundamental vector product for our surface is

$$
{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}=⟨-2{v}^{2},\,-4uv,\,-2{u}^{2}⟩.
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & =⟨2x,\,2y,\,z⟩{|}_{x={u}^{2}\,y=-uv\,z={v}^{2}} \\  & =⟨2{u}^{2},\,-2uv,\,{v}^{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the dot product of $F$ and ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨2{u}^{2},\,-2uv,\,{v}^{2}⟩\cdot ⟨-2{v}^{2},\,-4uv,\,-2{u}^{2}⟩ \\  & =2{u}^{2}\cdot (-2{v}^{2})+(-2uv)\cdot (-4uv)+{v}^{2}\cdot (-2{u}^{2}) \\  & =-4{u}^{2}{v}^{2}+8{u}^{2}{v}^{2}-2{u}^{2}{v}^{2} \\  & =2{u}^{2}{v}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\,2{u}^{2}{v}^{2}\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

last_observation.knowledge_point: Example: Expressing Flux Through a Surface as a Double Integral
last_observation.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A.
$$

Notice we are told that the fundamental vector product for our surface is

$$
{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}=⟨-2{v}^{2},\,-4uv,\,-2{u}^{2}⟩.
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & =⟨2x,\,2y,\,z⟩{|}_{x={u}^{2}\,y=-uv\,z={v}^{2}} \\  & =⟨2{u}^{2},\,-2uv,\,{v}^{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the dot product of $F$ and ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨2{u}^{2},\,-2uv,\,{v}^{2}⟩\cdot ⟨-2{v}^{2},\,-4uv,\,-2{u}^{2}⟩ \\  & =2{u}^{2}\cdot (-2{v}^{2})+(-2uv)\cdot (-4uv)+{v}^{2}\cdot (-2{u}^{2}) \\  & =-4{u}^{2}{v}^{2}+8{u}^{2}{v}^{2}-2{u}^{2}{v}^{2} \\  & =2{u}^{2}{v}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\,2{u}^{2}{v}^{2}\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

If the flux of F across S with respect to n is given by

For a surface S with parametrization r(u,v) for (u,v)∈D, the flux of a vector field F over S is given by

∬SF⋅dS=∬SF⋅ndS=∬DF(r(u,v))⋅(ru′×rv′)dA.

ru′×rv′=⟨−2v2,−4uv,−2u2⟩.

F(r(u,v))=⟨2x,2y,z⟩|x=u2y=−uvz=v2=⟨2u2,−2uv,v2⟩

∬SF⋅dS=∬DF(r(u,v))⋅(ru′×rv′)dA=∬D2u2v2dA.

{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{D}\boxed{}\,\text{d}A
$$

what is the missing expression?

*Hint: You can use the fact that ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}=⟨-2{v}^{2},\,-4uv,\,-2{u}^{2}⟩.$*
feedback.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A.
$$

Notice we are told that the fundamental vector product for our surface is

$$
{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}=⟨-2{v}^{2},\,-4uv,\,-2{u}^{2}⟩.
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & =⟨2x,\,2y,\,z⟩{|}_{x={u}^{2}\,y=-uv\,z={v}^{2}} \\  & =⟨2{u}^{2},\,-2uv,\,{v}^{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the dot product of $F$ and ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨2{u}^{2},\,-2uv,\,{v}^{2}⟩\cdot ⟨-2{v}^{2},\,-4uv,\,-2{u}^{2}⟩ \\  & =2{u}^{2}\cdot (-2{v}^{2})+(-2uv)\cdot (-4uv)+{v}^{2}\cdot (-2{u}^{2}) \\  & =-4{u}^{2}{v}^{2}+8{u}^{2}{v}^{2}-2{u}^{2}{v}^{2} \\  & =2{u}^{2}{v}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\,2{u}^{2}{v}^{2}\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

F(x,y,z)=⟨2x,2y,z⟩,r(u,v)=⟨u2,−uv,v2⟩,(u,v)∈D⊂R2.

If the flux of F across S with respect to n is given by

∬SF⋅dS=∬DAAAAAAAdA

what is the missing expression?

a

EXPLANATION

For a surface S with parametrization r(u,v) for (u,v)∈D, the flux of a vector field F over S is given by

∬SF⋅dS=∬SF⋅ndS=∬DF(r(u,v))⋅(ru′×rv′)dA.

Notice we are told that the fundamental vector product for our surface is

ru′×rv′=⟨−2v2,−4uv,−2u2⟩.

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of r(u,v) into F(x,y,z):

F(r(u,v))=⟨2x,2y,z⟩|x=u2y=−uvz=v2=⟨2u2,−2uv,v2⟩

question.name: Question 3
question.problem:
Consider the vector field $F$ and the surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v),$ where

$$
F(x,y,z)=⟨1,\,0,\,2⟩,\,r(u,v)=⟨u+v,\,{u}^{2}+2v,\,{u}^{3}+3v⟩,\,(u,v)\in D⊂{R}^{2}.
$$

If the flux of $F$ across $S$ with respect to $n$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{D}a{u}^{2}+bu+c\,\text{d}A
$$

what is the value of $a+b+c?$
question.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A.
$$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u+v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}({u}^{2}+2v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}({u}^{3}+3v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,2u,\,3{u}^{2}⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u+v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}({u}^{2}+2v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}({u}^{3}+3v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,2,\,3⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 2u & 3{u}^{2} \\ 1 & 2 & 3\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}2u & 3{u}^{2} \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & 3{u}^{2} \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 2u \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨6u-6{u}^{2},\,3{u}^{2}-3,\,2-2u⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & =⟨1,\,0,\,2⟩{|}_{x=u+v\,y={u}^{2}+2v\,z={u}^{3}+3v} \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,2⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the dot product of $F$ and ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨1,\,0,\,2⟩\cdot ⟨6u-6{u}^{2},\,3{u}^{2}-3,\,2-2u⟩ \\  & =1\cdot (6u-6{u}^{2})+0\cdot (3{u}^{2}-3)+2\cdot (2-2u) \\  & =6u-6{u}^{2}+4-4u \\  & =-6{u}^{2}+2u+4.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(-6)\cdot {u}^{2}+2\cdot u+4\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, 

$$
a+b+c=-6+2+4=0.
$$

If the flux of F across S with respect to n is given by

∬SF⋅dS=∬Dau2+bu+cdA

a

EXPLANATION

For a surface S with parametrization r(u,v) for (u,v)∈D, the flux of a vector field F over S is given by

∬SF⋅dS=∬SF⋅ndS=∬DF(r(u,v))⋅(ru′×rv′)dA.

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

ru′=⟨∂x∂u,∂y∂u,∂z∂u⟩=⟨∂∂u(u+v),∂∂u(u2+2v),∂∂u(u3+3v)⟩=⟨1,2u,3u2⟩rv′=⟨∂x∂v,∂y∂v,∂z∂v⟩=⟨∂∂v(u+v),∂∂v(u2+2v),∂∂v(u3+3v)⟩=⟨1,2,3⟩

Now, the fundamental vector product is

ru′×rv′=|ijk12u3u2123|=⟨|2u3u223|,−|13u213|,|12u12|⟩=⟨6u−6u2,3u2−3,2−2u⟩.

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of r(u,v) into F(x,y,z):

F(r(u,v))=⟨1,0,2⟩|x=u+vy=u2+2vz=u3+3v=⟨1,0,2⟩.

Finally, we calculate the dot product of F and ru′×rv′:

F(r(u,v))⋅(ru′×rv′)=⟨1,0,2⟩⋅⟨6u−6u2,3u2−3,2−2u⟩=1⋅(6u−6u2)+0⋅(3u2−3)+2⋅(2−2u)=6u−6u2+4−4u=−6u2+2u+4.

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

∬SF⋅dS=∬DF(r(u,v))⋅(ru′×rv′)dA=∬D(−6)⋅u2+2⋅u+4dA.

Finally,

a+b+c=−6+2+4=0.

last_observation.name: Question 3
last_observation.knowledge_point: Example: Expressing Flux Through a Surface as a Double Integral
last_observation.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A.
$$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u+v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}({u}^{2}+2v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}({u}^{3}+3v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,2u,\,3{u}^{2}⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u+v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}({u}^{2}+2v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}({u}^{3}+3v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,2,\,3⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 2u & 3{u}^{2} \\ 1 & 2 & 3\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}2u & 3{u}^{2} \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & 3{u}^{2} \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 2u \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨6u-6{u}^{2},\,3{u}^{2}-3,\,2-2u⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & =⟨1,\,0,\,2⟩{|}_{x=u+v\,y={u}^{2}+2v\,z={u}^{3}+3v} \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,2⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the dot product of $F$ and ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨1,\,0,\,2⟩\cdot ⟨6u-6{u}^{2},\,3{u}^{2}-3,\,2-2u⟩ \\  & =1\cdot (6u-6{u}^{2})+0\cdot (3{u}^{2}-3)+2\cdot (2-2u) \\  & =6u-6{u}^{2}+4-4u \\  & =-6{u}^{2}+2u+4.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(-6)\cdot {u}^{2}+2\cdot u+4\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, 

$$
a+b+c=-6+2+4=0.
$$

Question 3
?

Consider the vector field F and the surface S with parametrization r(u,v), where

F(x,y,z)=⟨1,0,2⟩,r(u,v)=⟨u+v,u2+2v,u3+3v⟩,(u,v)∈D⊂R2.

If the flux of F across S with respect to n is given by

∬SF⋅dS=∬Dau2+bu+cdA

what is the value of a+b+c?

a
2
b
−4
c
0
d
−2
e
4
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

For a surface S with parametrization r(u,v) for (u,v)∈D, the flux of a vector field F over S is given by

∬SF⋅dS=∬SF⋅ndS=∬DF(r(u,v))⋅(ru′×rv′)dA.

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

ru′=⟨∂x∂u,∂y∂u,∂z∂u⟩=⟨∂∂u(u+v),∂∂u(u2+2v),∂∂u(u3+3v)⟩=⟨1,2u,3u2⟩rv′=⟨∂x∂v,∂y∂v,∂z∂v⟩=⟨∂∂v(u+v),∂∂v(u2+2v),∂∂v(u3+3v)⟩=⟨1,2,3⟩

Now, the fundamental vector product is

ru′×rv′=|ijk12u3u2123|=⟨|2u3u223|,−|13u213|,|12u12|⟩=⟨6u−6u2,3u2−3,2−2u⟩.

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of r(u,v) into F(x,y,z):

F(r(u,v))=⟨1,0,2⟩|x=u+vy=u2+2vz=u3+3v=⟨1,0,2⟩.

Finally, we calculate the dot product of F and ru′×rv′:

F(r(u,v))⋅(ru′×rv′)=⟨1,0,2⟩⋅⟨6u−6u2,3u2−3,2−2u⟩=1⋅(6u−6u2)+0⋅(3u2−3)+2⋅(2−2u)=6u−6u2+4−4u=−6u2+2u+4.

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

∬SF⋅dS=∬DF(r(u,v))⋅(ru′×rv′)dA=∬D(−6)⋅u2+2⋅u+4dA.

Finally,

a+b+c=−6+2+4=0.

question.name: Question 4
question.problem:
Consider the vector field $F$ and the surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v),$ where

$$
F(x,y,z)=⟨2x+y,\,2z,\,y+z⟩,\,r(u,v)=⟨-{u}^{2},\,2{u}^{2}-{v}^{2},\,{v}^{2}⟩,\,(u,v)\in D⊂{R}^{2}.

If the flux of $F$ across $S$ with respect to $n$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{D}\boxed{}\,\text{d}A
$$

what is the missing expression?

*Hint: You can use the fact that ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}=⟨8uv,\,4uv,\,4uv⟩.$*

$$

Notice we are told that the fundamental vector product for our surface is

$$
{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}=⟨8uv,\,4uv,\,4uv⟩.
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & =⟨2x+y,\,2z,\,y+z⟩{|}_{x=-{u}^{2}\,y=2{u}^{2}-{v}^{2}\,z={v}^{2}} \\  & =⟨2(-{u}^{2})+(2{u}^{2}-{v}^{2}),\,2({v}^{2}),\,(2{u}^{2}-{v}^{2})+{v}^{2}⟩ \\  & =⟨-{v}^{2},\,2{v}^{2},\,2{u}^{2}⟩\end{aligned}

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨-{v}^{2},\,2{v}^{2},\,2{u}^{2}⟩\cdot ⟨8uv,\,4uv,\,4uv⟩ \\  & =(-{v}^{2})\cdot 8uv+2{v}^{2}\cdot 4uv+2{u}^{2}\cdot 4uv \\  & =-8u{v}^{3}+8u{v}^{3}+8{u}^{3}v \\  & =8{u}^{3}v.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\,8{u}^{3}v\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 4
?

Consider the vector field F and the surface S with parametrization r(u,v), where

F(x,y,z)=⟨2x+y,2z,y+z⟩,r(u,v)=⟨−u2,2u2−v2,v2⟩,(u,v)∈D⊂R2.

If the flux of F across S with respect to n is given by

∬SF⋅dS=∬DAAAAAAAdA

what is the missing expression?

Hint: You can use the fact that ru′×rv′=⟨8uv,4uv,4uv⟩.

a
8uv3+8u3v
b
8uv3
c
4uv3+2u3v
d
2uv3+4u3v
e
8u3v
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

For a surface S with parametrization r(u,v) for (u,v)∈D, the flux of a vector field F over S is given by

∬SF⋅dS=∬SF⋅ndS=∬DF(r(u,v))⋅(ru′×rv′)dA.

Notice we are told that the fundamental vector product for our surface is

ru′×rv′=⟨8uv,4uv,4uv⟩.

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of r(u,v) into F(x,y,z):

F(r(u,v))=⟨2x+y,2z,y+z⟩|x=−u2y=2u2−v2z=v2=⟨2(−u2)+(2u2−v2),2(v2),(2u2−v2)+v2⟩=⟨−v2,2v2,2u2⟩

Finally, we calculate the dot product of F and ru′×rv′:

F(r(u,v))⋅(ru′×rv′)=⟨−v2,2v2,2u2⟩⋅⟨8uv,4uv,4uv⟩=(−v2)⋅8uv+2v2⋅4uv+2u2⋅4uv=−8uv3+8uv3+8u3v=8u3v.

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

∬SF⋅dS=∬DF(r(u,v))⋅(ru′×rv′)dA=∬D8u3vdA.

Question 4

Consider the vector field F and the surface S with parametrization r(u,v), where

F(x,y,z)=⟨2x+y,2z,y+z⟩,r(u,v)=⟨−u2,2u2−v2,v2⟩,(u,v)∈D⊂R2.

If the flux of F across S with respect to n is given by

∬SF⋅dS=∬DAAAAAAAdA

what is the missing expression?

Hint: You can use the fact that ru′×rv′=⟨8uv,4uv,4uv⟩.

a
8uv3+8u3v
b
8uv3
c
4uv3+2u3v
d
2uv3+4u3v
e
8u3v
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

For a surface S with parametrization r(u,v) for (u,v)∈D, the flux of a vector field F over S is given by

∬SF⋅dS=∬SF⋅ndS=∬DF(r(u,v))⋅(ru′×rv′)dA.

Notice we are told that the fundamental vector product for our surface is

ru′×rv′=⟨8uv,4uv,4uv⟩.

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of r(u,v) into F(x,y,z):

F(r(u,v))=⟨2x+y,2z,y+z⟩|x=−u2y=2u2−v2z=v2=⟨2(−u2)+(2u2−v2),2(v2),(2u2−v2)+v2⟩=⟨−v2,2v2,2u2⟩

Finally, we calculate the dot product of F and ru′×rv′:

F(r(u,v))⋅(ru′×rv′)=⟨−v2,2v2,2u2⟩⋅⟨8uv,4uv,4uv⟩=(−v2)⋅8uv+2v2⋅4uv+2u2⋅4uv=−8uv3+8uv3+8u3v=8u3v.

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

∬SF⋅dS=∬DF(r(u,v))⋅(ru′×rv′)dA=∬D8u3vdA.

feedback.name: Question 4
feedback.problem:
Consider the vector field $F$ and the surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v),$ where

$$
F(x,y,z)=⟨2x+y,\,2z,\,y+z⟩,\,r(u,v)=⟨-{u}^{2},\,2{u}^{2}-{v}^{2},\,{v}^{2}⟩,\,(u,v)\in D⊂{R}^{2}.
$$

If the flux of $F$ across $S$ with respect to $n$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{D}\boxed{}\,\text{d}A
$$

what is the missing expression?

*Hint: You can use the fact that ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}=⟨8uv,\,4uv,\,4uv⟩.$*
feedback.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A.
$$

Notice we are told that the fundamental vector product for our surface is

$$
{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}=⟨8uv,\,4uv,\,4uv⟩.
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & =⟨2x+y,\,2z,\,y+z⟩{|}_{x=-{u}^{2}\,y=2{u}^{2}-{v}^{2}\,z={v}^{2}} \\  & =⟨2(-{u}^{2})+(2{u}^{2}-{v}^{2}),\,2({v}^{2}),\,(2{u}^{2}-{v}^{2})+{v}^{2}⟩ \\  & =⟨-{v}^{2},\,2{v}^{2},\,2{u}^{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the dot product of $F$ and ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨-{v}^{2},\,2{v}^{2},\,2{u}^{2}⟩\cdot ⟨8uv,\,4uv,\,4uv⟩ \\  & =(-{v}^{2})\cdot 8uv+2{v}^{2}\cdot 4uv+2{u}^{2}\cdot 4uv \\  & =-8u{v}^{3}+8u{v}^{3}+8{u}^{3}v \\  & =8{u}^{3}v.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\,8{u}^{3}v\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

question.name: Question 5
question.problem:
Consider the vector field $F$ and the surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v),$ where

$$
F(x,y,z)=⟨3x,\,3y,\,z⟩,\,r(u,v)=⟨u\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,u\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,{u}^{2}⟩,\,(u,v)\in D⊂{R}^{2}.

$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & =⟨3x,\,3y,\,z⟩{|}_{x=u\operatorname{cos}⁡v\,y=u\operatorname{sin}⁡v\,z={u}^{2}} \\  & =⟨3u\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,3u\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,{u}^{2}⟩\end{aligned}

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨3u\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,3u\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,{u}^{2}⟩\cdot ⟨-2{u}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,-2{u}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,u⟩ \\  & =3u\operatorname{cos}⁡v\cdot (-2{u}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡v)+3u\operatorname{sin}⁡v\cdot (-2{u}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡v)+{u}^{2}\cdot u \\  & =-6{u}^{3}({cos}^{2}⁡v+{sin}^{2}⁡v)+{u}^{3} \\  & =-5{u}^{3}.\end{aligned}

$$

question.html:
Question 5
?

Consider the vector field F and the surface S with parametrization r(u,v), where

F(x,y,z)=⟨3x,3y,z⟩,r(u,v)=⟨ucos⁡v,usin⁡v,u2⟩,(u,v)∈D⊂R2.

If the flux of F across S with respect to n is given by

∬SF⋅dS=∬DAAAAAAAdA

what is the missing expression?

Hint: You can use the fact that ru′×rv′=⟨−2u2cos⁡v,−2u2sin⁡v,u⟩.

a
−3u2
b
2u2sin⁡vcos⁡v
c
u3sin⁡vcos⁡v
d
−5u3
e
6u3
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

For a surface S with parametrization r(u,v) for (u,v)∈D, the flux of a vector field F over S is given by

∬SF⋅dS=∬SF⋅ndS=∬DF(r(u,v))⋅(ru′×rv′)dA.

Notice we are told that the fundamental vector product for our surface is

ru′×rv′=⟨−2u2cos⁡v,−2u2sin⁡v,u⟩.

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of r(u,v) into F(x,y,z):

F(r(u,v))=⟨3x,3y,z⟩|x=ucos⁡vy=usin⁡vz=u2=⟨3ucos⁡v,3usin⁡v,u2⟩

Finally, we calculate the dot product of F and ru′×rv′:

F(r(u,v))⋅(ru′×rv′)=⟨3ucos⁡v,3usin⁡v,u2⟩⋅⟨−2u2cos⁡v,−2u2sin⁡v,u⟩=3ucos⁡v⋅(−2u2cos⁡v)+3usin⁡v⋅(−2u2sin⁡v)+u2⋅u=−6u3(cos2⁡v+sin2⁡v)+u3=−5u3.

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

∬SF⋅dS=∬DF(r(u,v))⋅(ru′×rv′)dA=∬D−5u3dA.

question.html:
Question 5
?

Consider the vector field F and the surface S with parametrization r(u,v), where

F(x,y,z)=⟨3x,3y,z⟩,r(u,v)=⟨ucos⁡v,usin⁡v,u2⟩,(u,v)∈D⊂R2.

If the flux of F across S with respect to n is given by

∬SF⋅dS=∬DAAAAAAAdA

what is the missing expression?

Hint: You can use the fact that ru′×rv′=⟨−2u2cos⁡v,−2u2sin⁡v,u⟩.

a
−3u2
b
2u2sin⁡vcos⁡v
c
u3sin⁡vcos⁡v
d
−5u3
e
6u3
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

For a surface S with parametrization r(u,v) for (u,v)∈D, the flux of a vector field F over S is given by

∬SF⋅dS=∬SF⋅ndS=∬DF(r(u,v))⋅(ru′×rv′)dA.

Notice we are told that the fundamental vector product for our surface is

ru′×rv′=⟨−2u2cos⁡v,−2u2sin⁡v,u⟩.

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of r(u,v) into F(x,y,z):

F(r(u,v))=⟨3x,3y,z⟩|x=ucos⁡vy=usin⁡vz=u2=⟨3ucos⁡v,3usin⁡v,u2⟩

Finally, we calculate the dot product of F and ru′×rv′:

F(r(u,v))⋅(ru′×rv′)=⟨3ucos⁡v,3usin⁡v,u2⟩⋅⟨−2u2cos⁡v,−2u2sin⁡v,u⟩=3ucos⁡v⋅(−2u2cos⁡v)+3usin⁡v⋅(−2u2sin⁡v)+u2⋅u=−6u3(cos2⁡v+sin2⁡v)+u3=−5u3.

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

∬SF⋅dS=∬DF(r(u,v))⋅(ru′×rv′)dA=∬D−5u3dA.

feedback.name: Question 5
feedback.problem:
Consider the vector field $F$ and the surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v),$ where

$$
F(x,y,z)=⟨3x,\,3y,\,z⟩,\,r(u,v)=⟨u\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,u\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,{u}^{2}⟩,\,(u,v)\in D⊂{R}^{2}.
$$

If the flux of $F$ across $S$ with respect to $n$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{D}\boxed{}\,\text{d}A
$$

what is the missing expression?

*Hint: You can use the fact that ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}=⟨-2{u}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,-2{u}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,u⟩.$*
feedback.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A.
$$

Notice we are told that the fundamental vector product for our surface is

$$
{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}=⟨-2{u}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,-2{u}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,u⟩.
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & =⟨3x,\,3y,\,z⟩{|}_{x=u\operatorname{cos}⁡v\,y=u\operatorname{sin}⁡v\,z={u}^{2}} \\  & =⟨3u\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,3u\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,{u}^{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the dot product of $F$ and ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨3u\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,3u\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,{u}^{2}⟩\cdot ⟨-2{u}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,-2{u}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,u⟩ \\  & =3u\operatorname{cos}⁡v\cdot (-2{u}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡v)+3u\operatorname{sin}⁡v\cdot (-2{u}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡v)+{u}^{2}\cdot u \\  & =-6{u}^{3}({cos}^{2}⁡v+{sin}^{2}⁡v)+{u}^{3} \\  & =-5{u}^{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\,-5{u}^{3}\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

question.name: Question 6
question.problem:
Evaluate the surface integral

$$
{∬}_{S}⟨x,\,y,\,-z⟩\cdot \text{d}S
$$

where the parametric surface $S$ is defined by

$$
r(u,v)=⟨u+v,\,v-u,\,uv⟩
$$

over the domain $D=\{(u,v)\,:\,-2\le u\le 0,\,0\le v\le 1\}.$

*Hint: You can use the fact that ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}=⟨-u-v,\,v-u,\,2⟩.$*
question.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A.
$$

We're given that the fundamental vector product for our surface is

$$
{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}=⟨-u-v,\,v-u,\,2⟩.
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & ={⟨x,\,y,\,-z⟩|}_{x=u+v\,y=v-u\,z=uv} \\  & =⟨u+v,\,v-u,\,-uv⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we calculate the dot product of $F$ and ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨u+v,\,v-u,\,-uv⟩\cdot ⟨-u-v,\,v-u,\,2⟩ \\  & =(u+v)\cdot (-u-v)+(v-u)\cdot (v-u)+(-uv)\cdot 2 \\  & =-{u}^{2}-2uv-{v}^{2}+{v}^{2}-2uv+{u}^{2}-2uv \\  & =-6uv\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral evaluates to

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}⟨x,\,y,\,-z⟩\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(-6uv)\,\text{d}A \\  & =-6{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{-2}^{0}uv\,\text{d}u\,\text{d}v \\  & =-6{\int }_{0}^{1}v\,\text{d}v{\int }_{-2}^{0}u\,\text{d}u \\  & =-6\cdot [\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2}]_{0}^{1}\cdot {[\frac{1}{2}{u}^{2}]}_{-2}^{0} \\  & =-6\cdot \frac{1}{2}\cdot (-2) \\  & =6.\end{aligned}

?

Evaluate the surface integral

∬S⟨x,y,−z⟩⋅dS

where the parametric surface S is defined by

r(u,v)=⟨u+v,v−u,uv⟩

over the domain D={(u,v):−2≤u≤0,0≤v≤1}.

Hint: You can use the fact that ru′×rv′=⟨−u−v,v−u,2⟩.

6

For a surface S with parametrization r(u,v) for (u,v)∈D, the flux of a vector field F over S is given by

∬SF⋅dS=∬SF⋅ndS=∬DF(r(u,v))⋅(ru′×rv′)dA.

We're given that the fundamental vector product for our surface is

ru′×rv′=⟨−u−v,v−u,2⟩.

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of r(u,v) into F(x,y,z): F(r(u,v))=⟨x,y,−z⟩|x=u+vy=v−uz=uv=⟨u+v,v−u,−uv⟩

Then, we calculate the dot product of F and ru′×rv′: F(r(u,v))⋅(ru′×rv′)=⟨u+v,v−u,−uv⟩⋅⟨−u−v,v−u,2⟩=(u+v)⋅(−u−v)+(v−u)⋅(v−u)+(−uv)⋅2=−u2−2uv−v2+v2−2uv+u2−2uv=−6uv

∬S⟨x,y,−z⟩⋅dS=∬DF(r(u,v))⋅(ru′×rv′)dA=∬D(−6uv)dA=−6∫01∫−20uvdudv=−6∫01vdv∫−20udu=−6⋅[12v2]01⋅[12u2]−20=−6⋅12⋅(−2)=6.
